concepts.name: AI coding agents
concepts.definition: AI coding agents are assistants that can plan, edit files, run tools, and produce pull requests or other software changes with varying levels of autonomy.

concepts.name: Agentic workflows
concepts.definition: Agentic workflows use AI agents as active participants in software tasks such as triage, implementation, review, testing, deployment, and maintenance.

concepts.name: Human-in-the-loop oversight
concepts.definition: Human-in-the-loop oversight keeps people responsible for direction, approvals, exceptions, and final shipping decisions while agents do parts of the work.

concepts.name: Agent governance and permissions
concepts.definition: Agent governance and permissions define what agents are allowed to access, change, approve, or escalate so their work remains secure and auditable.

concepts.name: Multi-agent orchestration
concepts.definition: Multi-agent orchestration coordinates several specialized agents and handoff objects so complex work can move across roles, systems, or lifecycle stages.

concepts.name: Proactive agents
concepts.definition: Proactive agents decide what to do next without a direct prompt by using goals, memory, feedback, and review of prior work.

concepts.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
concepts.definition: Model Context Protocol is a standard way for AI tools and agents to connect to external services, data, and actions through tool servers.

concepts.name: MCP servers
concepts.definition: MCP servers expose tools, data, or documentation to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol.

concepts.name: MCP security
concepts.definition: MCP security covers the risks, exploit paths, hosting practices, and mitigations involved when agents can call external MCP tools.

concepts.name: Fine-grained MCP authorization
concepts.definition: Fine-grained MCP authorization limits which MCP tools and actions an agent may use for a particular user or context.

concepts.name: Agent skills
concepts.definition: Agent skills are reusable files that package instructions, workflows, and judgment so an agent can perform a recurring task consistently.

concepts.name: Skill discovery and management
concepts.definition: Skill discovery and management is the process of finding, evaluating, installing, updating, and distributing agent skills across developer environments.

concepts.name: Copilot customization layers
concepts.definition: Copilot customization layers are the configuration files, instructions, skills, agents, plugins, and connections that shape how Copilot behaves for a user, repo, team, or enterprise.

concepts.name: Custom agents and plugins
concepts.definition: Custom agents and plugins extend an AI assistant with domain-specific behavior, tools, or review checks beyond its built-in capabilities.

concepts.name: Copilot CLI workflows
concepts.definition: Copilot CLI workflows use agentic assistance from the terminal to automate coding, repository, review, documentation, or operational tasks.

concepts.name: Agent lifecycle hooks
concepts.definition: Agent lifecycle hooks let developers run custom actions when an agent starts working, becomes idle, errors, or reaches other lifecycle events.

concepts.name: Prompt assembly and context windows
concepts.definition: Prompt assembly and context windows describe how an AI tool selects files, conversation history, instructions, and other data to send to a model within its token limits.

concepts.name: Token usage optimization
concepts.definition: Token usage optimization reduces unnecessary prompt and context size so AI tools cost less and return more focused answers.

concepts.name: Developer knowledge bases
concepts.definition: Developer knowledge bases organize team artifacts such as issues, pull requests, docs, and discussions so agents can answer with project-specific context.

concepts.name: Retrieval grounding
concepts.definition: Retrieval grounding connects model responses to retrieved source material so answers can cite evidence and reduce unsupported guesses.

concepts.name: AI context as infrastructure
aliases: single source of truth for AI tools
concepts.definition: AI context as infrastructure treats instructions, skills, MCP servers, documentation, and configuration as managed platform assets shared across teams.

concepts.name: Coding model evaluations
concepts.definition: Coding model evaluations measure how well models perform real developer tasks, including task completion, correctness, regressions, speed, and user outcomes.

concepts.name: Release impact measurement
concepts.definition: Release impact measurement uses metrics, feature gates, experiments, and regression checks to decide whether a shipped change actually helped users.

concepts.name: Model routing and auto selection
concepts.definition: Model routing chooses which AI model or compute environment should handle a task based on quality, latency, cost, context, and capability needs.

concepts.name: Local and cloud models
concepts.definition: Local and cloud models combine on-device or self-hosted inference with hosted models so teams can balance privacy, cost, speed, and capability.

concepts.name: Open-weight coding models
concepts.definition: Open-weight coding models are downloadable or self-runnable code-focused models that teams can compare against hosted coding assistants for specific workloads.

concepts.name: Cloud agent sandboxes
concepts.definition: Cloud agent sandboxes provide isolated compute, repository access, identity, and permissions so agents can perform real work safely in the cloud.

concepts.name: Agent tracing and debugging
concepts.definition: Agent tracing records an agent's prompts, tool calls, errors, durations, and token use so teams can debug and improve its behavior.

concepts.name: AI adoption measurement
concepts.definition: AI adoption measurement connects AI tool usage to engineering, cost, quality, throughput, and business outcomes rather than only counting seats or hours saved.

concepts.name: Enterprise Copilot administration
concepts.definition: Enterprise Copilot administration covers the settings, access decisions, billing tools, policies, and reporting needed to operate Copilot across an organization.

concepts.name: AI fluency enablement
concepts.definition: AI fluency enablement helps teams progress from trying AI tools to reliably using agents and assistants in real delivery work.

concepts.name: GitHub Actions workflows
concepts.definition: GitHub Actions workflows are event-driven automation pipelines used to build, test, scan, deploy, or manage repository work.

concepts.name: CI/CD modernization
concepts.definition: CI/CD modernization updates legacy build and deployment pipelines to more maintainable, automated, governed, and agent-ready workflows.

concepts.name: GitHub Actions security hardening
concepts.definition: GitHub Actions security hardening reduces risk in workflows through safer defaults, least privilege, pinned dependencies, review controls, and runner protections.

concepts.name: Runner security
concepts.definition: Runner security protects the machines that execute CI/CD jobs, including their credentials, network access, updates, and isolation.

concepts.name: Dependency screening
concepts.definition: Dependency screening checks packages before they enter a build so malicious or compromised dependencies cannot execute with pipeline privileges.

concepts.name: Build egress control
concepts.definition: Build egress control records and restricts the external network destinations a build or workflow can contact.

concepts.name: Software supply chain security
concepts.definition: Software supply chain security protects the packages, build systems, CI/CD pipelines, credentials, artifacts, and release processes that software depends on.

concepts.name: Package provenance and OIDC
concepts.definition: Package provenance and OIDC let consumers verify where a package came from and whether it was built and published by the claimed workflow or identity.

concepts.name: Deterministic builds and manifests
concepts.definition: Deterministic builds and manifests make software contents reproducible and precisely knowable, enabling faster vulnerability detection and remediation.

concepts.name: Vulnerability reachability
concepts.definition: Vulnerability reachability shows whether an application's code can actually call vulnerable code, helping teams prioritize fixes.

concepts.name: Secret scanning and push protection
concepts.definition: Secret scanning and push protection detect credentials in code and block or route them before they enter repositories.

concepts.name: Security alert autofix
concepts.definition: Security alert autofix uses an agent to generate pull requests that remediate security findings, turning alert handling into reviewable code changes.

concepts.name: Actionable static analysis feedback
concepts.definition: Actionable static analysis feedback presents code quality or security findings in ways developers can trust, understand, and fix without excessive noise.

concepts.name: DevSecOps pipelines
concepts.definition: DevSecOps pipelines embed security scanning, policy checks, remediation, and auditability directly into development and delivery workflows.

concepts.name: Runtime observability
concepts.definition: Runtime observability watches software as it executes so teams can see processes, file access, network calls, errors, latency, and other live behavior.

concepts.name: Observability-driven agents
concepts.definition: Observability-driven agents use logs, traces, metrics, and service-level signals to diagnose issues, propose fixes, and verify changes under real conditions.

concepts.name: Incident RCA agents
concepts.definition: Incident RCA agents investigate alerts by gathering evidence, correlating signals, and producing structured root cause analyses for humans or downstream agents.

concepts.name: On-call agent autonomy
concepts.definition: On-call agent autonomy defines which incident-response decisions an agent may handle independently and which require trust gates or human approval.

concepts.name: Deployment runbooks and recovery automation
concepts.definition: Deployment runbooks and recovery automation encode approved operational steps so deployments and remediations can be repeated safely with oversight.

concepts.name: Self-validating agentic loops
concepts.definition: Self-validating agentic loops make the workflow that creates a change also produce evidence, tests, or checks proving the change works.

concepts.name: Automated test generation
concepts.definition: Automated test generation uses AI or automation to create, update, and run tests that validate new or changed behavior.

concepts.name: Browser-based agent testing
concepts.definition: Browser-based agent testing lets agents interact with applications like users, gather evidence, reproduce failures, and distinguish product issues from test or infrastructure issues.

concepts.name: Pull request review workflows
concepts.definition: Pull request review workflows combine human and automated review to evaluate diffs, enforce conventions, find bugs, and improve code before merge.

concepts.name: Stacked pull requests
concepts.definition: Stacked pull requests split a large change into ordered, dependent pull requests that can be reviewed and merged incrementally.

concepts.name: Plan-first review
concepts.definition: Plan-first review asks humans to evaluate the intended approach before an agent writes the diff, preserving collaboration and reducing late-stage review burden.

concepts.name: Specifications as hypotheses
concepts.definition: Specifications as hypotheses treats prompts and specs as testable assumptions that may need validation because model outputs vary across runs and versions.

concepts.name: Specification-driven development
concepts.definition: Specification-driven development starts with structured requirements or specs and uses agents, tests, and evidence to drive implementation toward verifiable outcomes.

concepts.name: Requirements from user feedback
concepts.definition: Requirements from user feedback uses AI to connect feedback channels, identify customer needs, and translate them into prioritized product requirements.

concepts.name: Prioritization as code
concepts.definition: Prioritization as code stores product assumptions, scoring rubrics, OKRs, and decisions in version-controlled files reviewed through pull requests.

concepts.name: Open roadmap collaboration
concepts.definition: Open roadmap collaboration uses public issues, discussions, project boards, and comments to shape product direction before code is written.

concepts.name: GitHub configuration as code
concepts.definition: GitHub configuration as code manages organization, repository, access, and policy settings as reviewed, version-controlled infrastructure changes.

concepts.name: Repository rulesets and branch protection
concepts.definition: Repository rulesets and branch protection enforce requirements such as reviews, checks, restrictions, and policies before changes can merge.

concepts.name: Identity-based agent authentication
concepts.definition: Identity-based agent authentication lets agents act on a user's behalf with scoped, short-lived credentials instead of copied long-lived secrets.

concepts.name: Signed evidence and audit trails
concepts.definition: Signed evidence and audit trails record who or what performed actions, what was approved, and what evidence supports a release or compliance decision.

concepts.name: Database branching
concepts.definition: Database branching creates isolated copies of schemas and data so agents and developers can test migrations or changes without risking production.

concepts.name: Legacy application modernization
concepts.definition: Legacy application modernization updates older applications through analysis, planning, refactoring, testing, dependency upgrades, vulnerability remediation, and migration.

concepts.name: Reproducible GitOps pipelines
concepts.definition: Reproducible GitOps pipelines use version-controlled desired state and automation to build, deploy, and audit systems in a repeatable way.

concepts.name: Accessibility automation
concepts.definition: Accessibility automation uses tools and AI to find, prevent, or fix accessibility issues while relying on humans for judgment and user impact.

concepts.name: Open source security governance
concepts.definition: Open source security governance covers the policies, reporting paths, triage practices, and community processes that help maintainers handle security responsibly.
